_note: Shared math+resolver fixture, asserted by rowver tests/test_core.py and rowver_web bin/stats/resolver/cutflow tests. Raw counts exact; weighted sums 1e-8 rtol; never bit parity. null in a value array means NaN; scalar 'nan'/'inf'/'-inf' strings mean those doubles. 'inf'/'-inf' strings in a weight array mean those doubles (a finite weight times a luminosity can overflow).

mask.note: NaN passes an inclusive range cut, like the page; hidden datasets drop

cutflow.note: column-order ladder (no session cutorder on the wire); range then chip; sources are gOf in first-appearance order
the page's own split: the ladder step tests lo <= x <= hi so NaN FAILS, while mask() rejects on x < lo || x > hi so NaN PASSES
a hidden sample is neither counted nor a source; its groupmate keeps the group alive
an unnarrowed cut is no cut; one 'no cuts' row equals the totals; ungrouped samples flow under their own names, first-appearance order
w accumulates left-to-right in row order (the page's +=): 1e16 absorbs the 8 until the -1e16 cancels; the surviving pair is exact
labels are the sankey's cutTextFor: num() grouping/exponential/6-sig rules for range bounds, JS string join for chips
select.ts:148 `(acc.by[g] || 0) + ww`: a NaN running by-total (inf + -inf) is falsy and resets to 0 before the next add, so a later weight un-poisons the column; the w total's sticky += stays NaN
ww is w × lumi composed by BOTH sides: group tier wins for mc1, sample tier reaches ungrouped mc2, and the unweighted dataset's rows count 1 — its sample-tier lumi entry must be ignored
